source.title: The Word Tariff
source.summary: How the Arabic ta'rif, meaning "to make known," became the most debated word in modern trade policy.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: In February 2025, the word "tariff" appeared in 847 news headlines in a single week. But where did this word come from? Travel back to 10th-century Alexandria, where transparent customs schedules called ta'rif revolutionized Mediterranean trade. Meet the Karimi merchants who built multinational trade networks, and discover how a word born from trade freedom became the vocabulary of trade protection.

linkedin.post: The etymology of economic terms often reveals forgotten truths about commerce. The word "tariff" — which dominated 847 news headlines in a single week this February — traces back to the Arabic "ta'rif," meaning "to make known." In 10th-century Alexandria, these were transparent customs schedules that revolutionized Mediterranean trade. The Karimi merchants used these clear pricing structures to build multinational trade networks. Everyone knew the costs upfront. Transparency enabled commerce. What began as a tool for trade freedom became the vocabulary of trade restriction. The same word that once meant clarity now fuels endless policy debates. Language carries the memory of economic history, even when we forget the lessons. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-tt-1
